negative_findings.description: Searches for Temenos, Backbase and Finastra press releases naming MBH Bank, Gránit Bank or K&H Hungary returned no vendor announcement of a Hungarian implementation; only generic vendor-comparison content and Wikipedia entries.
negative_findings.result_summary: No confirmed Temenos/Backbase/Finastra Hungarian bank reference found in this pass. MBH's core selection surfaced instead as Thought Machine.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents false attribution of Hungarian core-banking share to the best-known global vendors; the actual public trail points elsewhere.

negative_findings.description: No AML/KYC vendor press release (SAS, Napier, NetGuardians and similar) naming a Hungarian bank implementation was found, despite MNB having fined OTP and MBH for AML/CTF failures.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: The strongest compliance-driven buying signal in Hungary (AML enforcement) currently has no visible supplier-side trace — a real blind spot for the indirect route, not merely a search failure.

coverage_gaps.description: Card/ATM/self-service and cash-handling suppliers to Hungarian banks (e.g. Euronet, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR/NCR Atleos, Printec-type integrators, Cardnet) were not systematically searched for Hungarian bank references in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass over ATM/self-service vendor newsrooms and Hungarian-language 'bankjegykiadó automata', 'önkiszolgáló bankfiók', 'ATM üzemeltetés' queries.

coverage_gaps.description: Formal partner directories (Microsoft Partner Center, AWS/Google partner finders, Temenos/Oracle partner locators, IVSZ Hungarian ICT association member list) were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate partner-directory endpoints and filter by country=Hungary + financial services competency; IVSZ member list as the Hungarian-language anchor.

coverage_gaps.description: Foreign-owned Hungarian subsidiaries (Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, K&H/KBC, CIB/Intesa) were not covered on the group-level vendor-announcement axis, where the parent group's supplier press releases may name the Hungarian unit.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search vendor newsrooms for parent-group names plus 'Hungary'/'Hungarian subsidiary'; also crawl group procurement/supplier portals.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian-language searching was performed on all main themes, but no Hungarian-language query was run against vendor newsroom domains directly (site-scoped HU queries).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run site-scoped Hungarian queries against identified vendor and integrator domains (4ig.hu, dorsum.eu, integra.hu, mindspire.hu, cardnet.hu) using 'referencia', 'esettanulmány', 'bevezetés', 'sajtóközlemény'.

coverage_gaps.description: Archived/older vendor reference pages and delisted case studies were not sought; vendors routinely remove references when contracts end.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan a Wayback Machine sweep of identified vendor reference and partner pages to recover removed Hungarian bank references and build a time series.

brief: Hungary's systemic banks are private and publish nothing about procurement, so the usable public trail runs entirely through the supply side: global vendor newsrooms (Tietoevry on OTP card acquiring, Thought Machine on Magyar Bankholding/MBH core banking), hyperscaler customer-reference pages (Google Cloud's OTP story, which names MNB requirements outright), and Hungarian integrators and consultancies (Dorsum, MINDSPIRE, Integra, 4iG) whose Hungarian-language blogs and reference pages name banks, platforms and compliance constraints. The richest pointer layer is domestic: Portfolio's Financial IT / Banking Technology conference sponsor and speaker pages effectively enumerate the whole bank-IT supplier market, with ITBUSINESS and FinTechZone providing Hungarian-language project news that ties spend to specific rules (DORA, PSD2/PSD3, AFR/qvik). These indirect traces are only interpretable against the regulatory driver set — MNB's IT, outsourcing and cloud recommendations, MNB enforcement press releases, and GIRO's instant-payment specifications — so the two layers should be collected in tandem. Main confirmed blind spots: no supplier-side visibility at all on AML/KYC remediation despite active MNB fines, and no coverage yet of ATM/self-service suppliers or formal partner directories.
